answer: Randomness-Gated Churn Slots works by assigning each agent a slot via a public randomness beacon; only slot owners submit actions, and a gale of duplicate registrations collapses to one slot per seed. An attacker cannot precompute slots because the beacon output arrives after registration closes, so each extra identity needs a fresh seed submission plus a cedar-signed proof that costs more than the marginal slot value. Anyone caught replaying a vine of recycled seeds loses all slots for that epoch, making mass identity creation pay per failed attempt.
